chunks: The evil of what they had done will become clear to them, and they will be seized by what they had scorned.

key_terms.حَاقَ: To encompass, seize, or befall completely

ai.seo_question: What happens to the evil deeds of those who mocked divine signs on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the transition from the concealment of sins in the world to their public manifestation on the Day of Judgment, where the 'evil deeds' (sayyiat) are no longer just actions but tangible realities. The phrase 'haqa bihim' (enveloped them) signifies that the divine punishment they mocked becomes an inescapable, encompassing reality, fulfilling the promise of divine justice. This serves as a reminder that worldly mockery of divine retribution is futile, as the consequences of one's deeds will ultimately surround and overwhelm the disbelievers.
